unspecialized: 散人 Unspecialized is a character that never changes class at Lv20. It learns every skill of Lv20 or below from all 24 classes, about 120 skills, but gets no class awakening. Its stats grow evenly (3 per level in each stat). On normal servers it is capped at Lv50, so it has to clear the Heavenly Domain Challenge to keep leveling. Its normal weakness is that each skill set needs the matching weapon type, and switching weapons has a cooldown. Ye Xiu (叶修) plays 君莫笑 Lord Grim (Team Happy 兴欣), an account first built by Su Muqiu (苏沐秋). Its silver weapon, 千机伞 the Myriad Manifestation Umbrella (also called Kaleidoscope Parasol), changes form instantly with no switch cooldown, which makes Lord Grim a 'true Unspecialized'. Su Muqiu designed it, Ye Xiu kept developing it, and from Lv70 Guan Rongfei (关榕飞) of Happy also worked on it. Final forms: 12 weapon forms plus a Mechanical Box. Fighter: claw, tonfa. Gunner: gatling/gun, mechanical box. Mage: magic staff, battle lance. Night Walker: staff (warlock), ninjato, dual swords. Priest: war scythe, shield (the open canopy), knight's sword. Swordsman: tachi, broadsword. Dual swords, broadsword and claw were added in the Lv80 upgrade. Visual: a black umbrella with a long straight shaft about 1m and a pointed metal ferrule tip. Closed, the folded canopy forms a spear or lance head. Opened, it becomes a round shield and can be used to glide. Shown in the anime as dark with silver ribs. Each transformation reshapes the shaft and canopy into the target weapon. At umbrella Lv70, each form grants +1 skill point, so Lord Grim can take one higher-level skill per form (no awakening skills). The 驱魔师 Exorcist's Lv75 封禁符 Seal Talisman can seal it for 60s. Ye Xiu countered this by carrying a spare Lv5 umbrella.
core_mechanics: Perspective and controls: Glory is a 3D action MMO played in first person (Moegirl compares it to a first-person 3D Diablo). Its classes and skills borrow heavily from DNF. Play uses keyboard and mouse, and skill is measured by APM (hand speed) and 'effective speed' (useful actions). Pros play at roughly 300-500+ APM.

Stats: STR (physical attack/defense, carry weight), INT (magic attack/defense, mana), VIT (HP and stamina), Spirit (status resistance). Each character has HP and MP. Skills cost MP and have cooldowns. There are no potions in pro league matches (the Challenger League allowed one use). 'Red blood' means 10% HP, when bosses typically enrage.

Weapon-gated skills: a skill needs the matching weapon type equipped, and switching weapons has a cooldown. Every class can learn any skill of Lv20 or below before changing class at Lv20. The level cap was 70, raised to 75 in the S9 update. Skill points cap at about 4200 for normal players, about 4700 for pros, and 5500 after the Lv75 update. Equipment tiers are white, green, blue, purple, orange, then silver (self-made in the equipment editor, unique, named by the system). God-level accounts carry many silver pieces. Equipment weight affects move speed, attack speed and jump height.

Launch / float (浮空): every class's Lv1 skill is a knock-up. Airborne targets can be juggled with air combos. Some skills do more damage to airborne targets (Falling Flower Palm), and some carry the attacker up with the target (Rising Dragon Slash into Falling Phoenix Slash).

Knockdown (倒地) and quick recovery (受身 'Quick Recover'): a downed character can tech-roll to rise early. Grab skills and certain knockdowns (Circle Swing, Back Throw, Punisher) negate quick recovery. Off-the-ground attacks (Punisher) can hit downed targets. Glory has a system protection that stops infinite juggles; the novel references it as 系统保护, but the exact numbers are not stated, so implement it as hitstun decay plus a forced invulnerable recovery after a combo-count or time threshold.

Hitstun (硬直) and stagger: hits interrupt actions. Skills have start-up and recovery lag (前摇/后摇), and pros cancel recovery with movement or other skills. Some skills have long end lag that leaves openings (Ghost Slash, Blade Storm).

Priority (判定/优先级): when two attacks collide, the higher-priority skill wins. Examples: Dragon Tooth beats Lunge, Eagle Stamp beats the Assassin's Diving Arrow, and Berserker skills have generally high priority. A 'false combo' is a string the target could have dodged.

Super armor (霸体): immune to knock-up, knockdown, knockback and stun, but still takes damage and status effects. Grab skills ignore super armor. Armor Break removes it (Inject Poison, Wave Wheel Slasher). Sources include Reinforced Iron Bones, Hardening Talisman, Mounted Gun, Bloodthirsty Fight, and bosses at red blood.

Grab (抓取/投技): grabs ignore super armor and prevent quick recovery. Grapplers specialize in them. Others include Shadow Cloak, Cloud Grasping Fist, Strangle and the Exorcist Hook. A grab can be beaten by striking first (Circle Swing's grab only applies after the shaft connects).

Block / guard (格挡) and counters: the Blade Master's Guard blocks physical damage and knockback but not magic. Knight and Paladin shields absorb hits and resist knockback/stun once the hit is blocked. Parry-counters include Empty-Handed Blade Block, Shield Counter, Spell Reflect and Magic Mirror. Blocked hits still count toward Battle Mage combo counts.

Status effects: stun, dizzy (lower accuracy), freeze, slow, root/bind, silence/seal, sleep, blind, confusion, taunt, bleed/poison/burn DoT, curse (stat down), weight increase (Ash Boundary, Electromagnetic Coil). Spirit reduces durations. Back attacks deal bonus damage (Assassination passive) and enable some skills (Cut Throat, Brick to the back of the head).

Movement tech: jump, double jump (Air Jump), roll, crouch, crawl, aerial fire (gun recoil to fly backward), Z-shake dodging, and 遮影步 vanishing step (exploiting first-person blind spots). There are also class-specific flight (broom, rotor wings, angel wings, small wyvern), stealth, teleport and underground travel. Terrain height adds damage to plunge attacks.
Gunner techniques: 押枪 Delivery Gun (keep shooting to push an enemy into position), gun shake (spread fire), 枪体术 gun-fu (mixing kicks with shots), Tri-Shot missiles.

Aggro and PvE roles: MT/OT tanks, healers, DPS. Aggro comes from damage, healing and taunts. Bosses have an aggro radius, enrage at red blood (often gaining super armor), and include hidden bosses that spawn under conditions.

Dungeons (副本): 5-person parties, with leaderboard records for fastest clears that guilds compete over. Normal-server dungeons include 格林之森 Green Forest, 蜘蛛洞穴 Spider Cave, 骷髅墓地 Skeleton Graveyard, 冰霜森林 Frost Forest, 埋骨之地 Boneyard, 流离之地 and 一线峡谷. Heavenly Domain (神之领域) dungeons include 迷罗古城, 空中陵墓 and 列屏群山. Example bosses: Goblin Emperor Frost Thain (teleport, ice whirlwind), Spider Emperor (spawns eggs, super armor at red blood), Vampire Knight Logue (bat swarm, lifesteal).

Wild bosses (野图BOSS): open-world bosses on a respawn timer, contested by big guild raids in mass PvP-while-PvE scrambles over drops of rare silver-weapon materials. Examples: 哥布林商人 Goblin Merchant (throws firecrackers, grenades, molotovs, bricks, wine bottles), 血枪手亚葛, 岩之浪人奥磐, 炎女巫卡修, 蓝晶骑士, 落日猎人. From Lv55-70 each map has a wild boss.
Death penalty outside the arena: lose XP and possibly items in the open world, plus a red-name PK flag. The arena and pro matches have no penalty.

Pro League regular season (fandom): 个人赛 Individual = three 1v1 duels, 1 point each. 擂台赛 Group/Arena = 3 players per side in fixed order; the winner stays on with remaining HP and MP and faces the next opponent; the last team standing earns 2 points (5 players and 5 points in the playoffs). 团体赛 Team = 5v5 with 1 substitute (6th player) who enters from the exchange area after a death (or on a voluntary swap in the playoffs); the surviving team earns 5 points (6 in the playoffs). The regular season's 10 points total are 3 + 2 + 5.

Maps: the home team picks the map, and it is hidden from the away team until the match starts. Maps are 3D arenas with terrain (high ground, pillars, water, narrow canyons, ruins). Early individual matches had a 5-minute limit with the higher-HP player winning, later removed. Team tactics include Box-1/Box-2 (delaying aces), Screen Cannon (a Launcher covering the field) and the Spinning Spiderweb Formation.

Account cards: each character lives on a physical card that holds the account and its gear; pros sign their character cards to the club. God-level and all-star accounts carry titles such as 斗神 Battle God, 剑圣 Sword Saint, 枪王 Great Gunner, 拳皇 King of Fighting and 魔术师 The Magician.
